title: Affinity contingency lanes and variant-throttling playbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a deterministic playbook for routing tenant traffic to dedicated GPU capacity with graceful, cost- and latency-aware spillover to hosted endpoints and lower-cost variant models. The goal is to provide predictable SLO behavior for committed customers while ensuring platform-wide availability during regional pressure. This ticket covers policy definitions, throttling heuristics, token-reservation lanes, variant demotion order, and observability hooks needed for safe rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Routing adjudicator enforces per-tenant soft-reserve lanes and a fallback priority queue (dedicated -> quantized-variant -> hosted-backfill)
Circuit-breaker thresholds per-region evaluated and exercised in staging with synthetic bursts
End-to-end metrics emitted: spillover_rate, lane_utilization, variant_demotions, avg_tail_latency per-tenant and per-region
Canary rollout plan exists and feature-flag gates implemented for 10%/50%/100% ramps
Runbook updated with escalation steps and rollback criteria
tasks: Draft policy spec (region affinity, tiering, soft-reserve algorithm) and review with SRE and PM
Implement routing adjudicator changes (server-side) and token-bucket soft-reserve for P0/P1 tenants
Add variant demotion controller that prefers lower-cost quantized variants before hosted spillover
Integrate per-tenant throttles and hysteresis windows to avoid oscillation during bursty loads
Instrument metrics and dashboards; add alerting rules for spillover anomalies
Run staging soak and chaos tests; prepare canary and rollback playbooks
decisions: Use soft-reserve buckets (token leaky bucket) sized by tenant commit rather than hard capacity locks to maximize utilization
Demotion order: full model -> 8-bit quantized variant -> smaller-architecture variant -> hosted-backfill. Hosted overflow should carry strict per-tenant rate caps to limit cost exposure
Region selection: primary affinity by geo then latency; use hysteresis (30s ramp-down) to avoid flapping when evaluating failover
Circuit breaker rules evaluated by moving-window P95 latency and successful token drain; set initial thresholds to 2x target SLO for canary
Fallbacks are stateful-aware: KV-cache preservation attempts before demotion; if cache loss expected, prefer hosted variant with warm-warm routing when available
comments: 2025-11-16 - Asha Patel: Initial spec uploaded. Key open questions: how aggressive should soft-reserve be for mid-tier (P2) tenants? Put this up for SRE review.
2025-11-17 - SRE (Jordan Lee): Recommend starting with 20% of committed qps as soft-reserve for P1 and 10% for P2; avoid >30% reservation to keep utilization healthy.

2025-11-18 - Dmitri Volkov: Implemented prototype token-bucket in staging branch. Preliminary soak shows reduced tail latency for P0 tenants under synthetic 5x burst. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1824
2025-11-19 - PM (Riley Thomas): Confirmed customer priority mapping and legal constraints for hosted fallback (some tenants disallow hosted). Adding tenant flag 'hosted_allowed' to policy.
2025-11-20 - Design (Sofia Nguyen): UX note — dashboard should clearly surface 'why' a request spilled (quota vs capacity vs hysteresis). Added mockups in Confluence link above.
2025-11-21 - QA (Priya Singh): Found race when tearing down soft-reserve during region evacuation; added a test case. Marked as blocker for 50% canary ramp.
decisions_notes: Trade-offs considered: hard reservations guarantee latency but reduce overall throughput and increase costs. Soft-reserve balances guarantees and utilization, but requires robust telemetry to catch starving tenants.
We opted to prefer quantized variants over hosted fallback to limit cross-billing unpredictability and reduce variance in tail latency due to network egress.
Hysteresis window tuned to 30s after spike testing — shorter windows caused oscillation during synthetic traffic patterns.
next_steps: Merge routing PR after addressing QA race conditions
Deploy canary (10%) in us-west-2 with feature flag and monitor 'spillover_rate' and 'variant_demotions' over 48h
Coordinate with sales/CS to identify tenants with 'hosted_allowed=false' so we exclude them from hosted fallback
Prepare runbook tabletop exercise for SRE and Support with 3 failure modes: regional overload, cache-loss demotion, network egress spikes
last_update_summary: Prototype token-bucket soft-reserve implemented in staging. UX and PM feedback incorporated. QA found a teardown race; blocked on fix before canary. Instrumentation and dashboards mostly complete.
